title: 結局 — in the end, after all
summary: An adverb meaning that after various turns or hesitation, things ended up a certain way. Placed at the start of a sentence or before the predicate. The outcome is often not the one hoped for.

patterns.gloss: 結局 + past or negative verb

body.p: 結局 gives the conclusion that settled after much thought or many events. It is mostly in the past tense, in patterns like いろいろ～が、結局～ and ～たが、結局～.
最後に is the last in an order; ついに is when something long awaited finally happens. 結局 can describe outcomes that differ from hopes or plans. 結局のところ means 'in short.'

examples.ja: いろいろ考（かんが）えたが、結局（けっきょく）行（い）かないことにした。
examples.romaji: Iroiro kangaeta ga, kekkyoku ikanai koto ni shita.
examples.tr: I thought a lot, but in the end decided not to go.

examples.ja: 迷（まよ）ったが、結局（けっきょく）赤（あか）いかばんを選（えら）んだ。
examples.romaji: Mayotta ga, kekkyoku akai kaban o eranda.
examples.tr: I hesitated, but in the end I chose the red bag.

examples.ja: 一日（いちにち）中（じゅう）探（さが）したが、結局（けっきょく）鍵（かぎ）は見（み）つからなかった。
examples.romaji: Ichinichijū sagashita ga, kekkyoku kagi wa mitsukaranakatta.
examples.tr: I searched all day, but in the end I couldn't find the key.

pitfalls: It is awkward for future plans: 結局明日行く is unnatural. Use it after the outcome is settled.
ついに is for a hoped-for result; 結局 can be neutral or disappointing.
